swarm_roles.decision: Every ZECP01..ZECP20 process receives at least positive and hard-negative TRAIN coverage; composites test transfer.
Keep the 216-row S3 pack only for genuine local ternary gates; do not use it as a universal cognitive representation.
Add structured multi-step candidates for reconstruction, planning, Hyperposition, GWT, Claude bridge, effects/recovery, ClayCode and J-Space.

caught: shared execution/model-family/orchestration ancestry counted as independent evidence

swarm_roles.decision: Separate process-semantic correctness from binder correctness so a binding improvement cannot hide planning/recovery regressions.
Dual curriculum accepted as SOURCE_DESIGN_ONLY: Lane A pure binder (existing repo work), Lane B process trajectories (new artifact), Lane C selective binder composition (new artifact).

research_feedback.strongest_new_design_rule: Train and score three separable capabilities: semantic process transition, episode-local opaque binding, and their selective composition. Never let final-symbol accuracy substitute for process correctness.
research_feedback.counterhypothesis: The small 0.8B model may experience interference when architecture-process trajectories and binder overlays are mixed too early.
research_feedback.discriminator: Run staged curriculum ablation: binder-only vs trajectories-only vs staged dual curriculum vs mixed-from-start, holding token budget fixed; score pure-binding, atomic-process, composite-process, recovery, authority-integrity and off-target retention separately.
research_feedback.falsifier: Reject the dual-curriculum recipe if composition gains require regression in atomic process correctness, authority integrity, or pure binding generalization.

next_exact_gate: Bind exact selected Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint/tokenizer and verified ABI atoms; materialize Lane-A/C opaque atoms with token/last-position matching, convert Lane-B targets to the frozen training schema, run family/provenance leakage and authority lint, then perform a fixed-budget curriculum-order ablation before any large-scale corpus expansion.
